title: Validate PostHog UUIDT invocation IDs by shape rather than RFC UUID version
answers: Why does cancelling a workflow run fail with a validation error?
How to validate PostHog invocation IDs or UUIDTs in Zod schemas?
Workflow row Cancel action fails with validation error and run keeps going
Why does z.string().uuid() reject PostHog invocation_ids?
body:
Symptom: Cancelling a running workflow via the row Cancel action or direct API call fails with a validation error, and the run keeps going.
Root cause: nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:CdpApi used version-aware z.string().uuid() on invocation_ids, which rejects PostHog UUIDTs because their version nibbles do not conform to RFC UUID versions.
Fix pattern: Validate UUID string shape (8-4-4-4-12) using UUID.validateString(id, false) via z.string().refine() to accept UUIDTs while rejecting malformed inputs before Postgres ::uuid[] binds.
Constraints: Applies to route validation for PostHog UUIDT identifiers destined for Postgres UUID columns; does not apply when external contracts strictly require RFC-versioned UUIDs.
applies: PostHog CDP API route schema validation for workflow invocation IDs and UUIDTs.
